events.text:
**Recommendation: go to Grand Haven.** Fish 50–90 ft down over 85–150 ft of water. Run blue and green spoons and a white flasher-fly combo.

The newest reports are from 2026-08-12, which is 6 days old. They are the DNR's most recent weekly bulletin for each port.

| Port | My rating (0–4) | Newest report (2026-08-12) |
|---|---|---|
| **Grand Haven** | **3 (good)** | Rated 3 (good). Salmon were 50–90 ft down in 85–150 ft of water. Blue and green spoons worked, plus a white flasher-fly combo. |
| **South Haven** | **2 (average)** | Rated 2 (average). "A fair number" of salmon were 45–90 ft down in 100–130 ft of water. Green or blue glow spoons worked. |
| **St. Joseph** | **2 (low confidence)** | Not rated, so a weak positive. Salmon and a few steelhead were 55–80 ft down in 90–120 ft of water. White flasher-fly combos and glow spoons got the most bites. |
| **Muskegon** | **1 (below average)** | Rated 0 (slow). Salmon were marked 50–85 ft down in 100–140 ft of water, but anglers were "unsuccessful due to warm water." Glow spoons and glow plugs were best in low light. |

**Evidence**
- **Grand Haven:** Boat fishing was also good on 2026-07-22, with Chinook in 30–90 ft of water on green, blue and white spoons (Grand Haven, 2026-07-22). The pier was dead because of warm water (Grand Haven, 2026-08-12).
- **Muskegon:** The week before it was average, with decent Chinook from the pierheads out to 80 ft (Muskegon, 2026-07-22). Its slide to slow looks tied to warming water.
- **Water temperature:** Buoy surface temperatures this past week averaged about 72–74 F at every port, up about 1 F over the week. That is measured data. (Buoy summary, week before 2026-08-18.)

**History (earlier seasons, same calendar window)**
- Grand Haven boat fishing was rated good in mid-to-late August in 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Examples are 2025-08-20 (50–100 ft down in 80–220 ft of water) and 2025-08-13.
- South Haven and St. Joseph were often slow around this date. South Haven was slow on 2025-08-13 and 2025-08-20, and St. Joseph was slow on 2025-08-13, 2025-08-20 and 2023-08-23.
- Muskegon varied from year to year.
- When the surface temperature dropped sharply (a possible upwelling), fish often moved in shallower. For example, Muskegon and Grand Haven were good from the pierheads out to 90–100 ft on 2024-08-21 (surface down 14 F), and Muskegon was good in 50–120 ft on 2023-08-16.

**My read**
- With surface water in the low 70s, I'd expect salmon to stay deep, around 50–90 ft down, as they did in the reports.
- I'd expect Grand Haven to stay the most reliable. It has been good in the last two reports and in most past Augusts.
- I'd expect South Haven to stay middling.
- I'd expect St. Joseph to be the shakiest of the four. Its latest report has no rating, and it was often slow at this time of year in past seasons.
- Muskegon could rebound if cooler water arrives, but I wouldn't count on it this week.

**Caveats**
- Live conditions were unavailable. I have no wind or wave forecast, no modeled cold-layer depth, and no pierhead temperatures. Check the marine forecast before you go. If it's strong (20+ mph), stay in.
- A north or east wind that cools the surface would likely bring fish shallower, toward the pierheads. That is general guidance from Michigan Sea Grant/MSU Extension, not something the reports said.
- The ratings are my judgment, based on one week of reports plus history.
